# Untying Prefill and Decode Loops in Looped Language Models

> Looped (recurrent-depth) language models run one block of layers several times per token and, at inference, run the
> same number of loops to prefill the prompt and to decode each answer token. This work unties the two with a small
> loop adapter (LoRA + per-loop RoPE-commuting KV maps on a frozen model; one set of parameters for all 16 pairs of
> prefill loops m and decode loops n up to four) and measures what each count buys on Ouro-2.6B, Ouro-1.4B,
> Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, Ouro-1.4B-Thinking, SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview and Lev looped decision models. The paper's statistics
> are recomputed from released per-item scores by ouro/scripts/paper_numbers.py.

Main findings (95% paired bootstrap intervals in the paper; Ouro base-model evaluation settings where available):
- Decode cheaply, prefill deeply: on Ouro-2.6B with one decode loop, prefilling with four loops raises the average over
  11 benchmarks from 44.2 (native 1/1) to 56.8 (49.8 for native 1/1 distilled with LoRA on the same data); with two
  decode loops the adapter averages 67.2, within 3 points of native 4/4. Two to four prefill loops are best on 14 of
  15 settings at one decode loop; few-shot MATH-500 is the exception.
- Aligned caches (decode loop k reads prefill loop m-n+k) match the native model at equal depth and decode at about the
  cost of native n/n; one stored prompt cache (RoPE-commuting key scale on the query) gives up under one point.
- Without the adapter the same untied configurations average 26.6 and 30.9; 6M training tokens reach most of the
  48M result; three training seeds agree within 0.2.
- Ouro-2.6B-Thinking: prefill 4 / decode 2 matches native 4/4's average accuracy over eight benchmarks at 3.2x its
  decode throughput (one cache) and answers 192 timed GSM8K problems in 0.59x the time at batch 1.
- Lev looped decision models, both directions: more prefill than decision loops is significantly above a matched
  control on 12 of 13 (m, n) pairs; fewer is below it on all 13 (significantly 11).

Limitations stated by the author: the prefill count is calibrated per benchmark, not routed per prompt; the gain is
largest at low decode depth; with three or four decode loops the aligned adapter matches but does not beat native; on
Ouro-1.4B a distilled 2/2 is stronger on BBH, MATH-500 and RULER-16K; more prefill loops raise time to first token.

## Docs
- README.md: findings, when to use, repository map
- REPRODUCE.md: every table and figure -> script -> result file; training and evaluation commands
- paper/untying-prefill-decode-loops.pdf: the paper
- ouro/results/items/: per-item scores of every run the paper uses; ouro/results/paper_numbers.json: the recomputed statistics
- ouro/results/provenance/: command, configuration, checkpoint hash, log and outputs of every run
